# The Question Mythos and Daybreak Don't Answer

OpenAI and Google built AI that finds vulnerabilities. Nobody's answered the operational question: who runs these across 10,000 assets?

May 13, 2026, 2 min read, Alexander Semien, Head of Growth

OpenAI shipped Daybreak on Sunday, a frontier-model harness built on GPT-5.5 and Codex. Pointed at a code repository, it produces an editable threat model, runs candidate vulnerabilities in an isolated environment, and proposes fixes. My initial reaction was that frontier models have been able to do this for over a year, and what OpenAI actually shipped is a domain-specific harness with distinct marketing around it.

That marketing is anchored with launch partners - Akamai, Cisco, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, Fortinet, Oracle, Palo Alto Networks, and Zscaler - eight of the biggest names in cybersecurity lined up for day one, with a press cycle to match. Daybreak isn't really a cybersecurity product launch so much as a positioning play: OpenAI claiming the role of premier AI partner to cybersecurity, oriented around defense and distributed through the established security stack, with a pitch that boils down to **what the model can do for you**.

# Cogent's Head of Growth, Alexander Semien, breaks down the diverging narrative of AI-in-cybersecurity across two of the frontier labs. | Cogent · LinkedIn · 2026-05-13

**Cogent**: Cogent has 40-50 employees, founded in 2024. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, United States. Its workforce is distributed across United States and India. Has $53M in total funding, with 2 prior funding rounds.

---

[Cogent](https://linkedin.com/company/cogentsecurity)'s Head of Growth, [Alexander Semien](https://linkedin.com/in/alexander-semien), breaks down the diverging narrative of AI-in-cybersecurity across two of the frontier labs.

Yesterday's announcement from [OpenAI](https://linkedin.com/company/openai) positioned Daybreak as a defensive partnership story with legacy cybersecurity companies. [Anthropic](https://linkedin.com/company/anthropicresearch)'s Mythos, however, landed as offensive proof of maturing models - with early access given exclusively to mega-enterprises.

Both rest on the same underlying capabilities, and both stop short of the actual hard part: turning findings into fixes, on the time scale modern adversaries operate on.

Check out the original post and comments for the link!

Cue the (unnecessary) panic! Google Threat Intelligence Group attributed a zero-day to AI-assisted development. So, naturally, i'm back with another take on viral cyber news.

Anyone who's been watching the AI x Security space recently is thoroughly unsurprised in the model capability. That said, the in-the-wild attribution and bug class are worth slowing down on.

GTIG calls it a semantic logic flaw. In plain terms: code that does what it was coded to do while quietly contradicting what it was supposed to do. The flaw lives in the gap between two functions that each look reasonable on their own. In this case, 2FA got bypassed and the adversary had an exploitable path in.

SAST and DAST aren't going to catch that. They're coded to look for specific things. Frontier LLMs were trained for cognition.

# Your scanner reports 25 CVEs. Your engineer needs to install one KB patch on 40 servers. | Cogent · LinkedIn · 2026-05-12

**Cogent**: Cogent has 40-50 employees, founded in 2024. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, United States. Its workforce is distributed across United States and India. Has $53M in total funding, with 2 prior funding rounds.

---

Your scanner reports 25 CVEs. Your engineer needs to install one KB patch on 40 servers.

Those are two very different units of work, and most VM programs force the security team to bridge that gap manually. Write up the remediation instructions, guess at the Jira project and assignee, follow up when the ticket goes stale, take the engineer's word when they mark it done.

The new Cogent Action Queue introduces Work Items: findings grouped by their shared remediation action, scoped to affected assets, with ownership resolved and instructions attached. One unit an engineer can execute without additional research.

[Haris Sohail](https://linkedin.com/in/haris-sohail) wrote up the full release on the blog (link in comments).
